title: Sample 17-16: Crossed-Out Letters and Equals Sign

illustrates.quote: Mathematical Symbols. Spellers often use mathematical symbols to teach word formation. a. Transcribe all text in word formation “equations” in uncontracted braille. b. If the result of the equation is a complete word, add the contracted form of the word at the end of the equation, enclosed in transcriber's note indicators.

blocks.text: Words with crossed-out letters are uncontracted, then repeated with a hyphen substituted for each crossed-out letter. The repeated word is enclosed within transcriber’s note indicators.

print.notes: A centred all-caps heading, a standalone transcriber's note (the same 17.11.1d/17.11.2c wording, reused here per 17.13.1b's own 'enclosed in transcriber's note indicators'), then six contraction equations combining the crossed-out-letter hyphen convention (§17.11) with an equals sign (17.13.1).
print.printFeatures: Centred all-caps heading; crossed-out letters combined with equations.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille unchanged. illustrates.rule: kept B's '17.13.1' over A's stacked '17.12.2, 17.13.1' — the source's own explicit cross-reference for THIS sample sits at the end of 17.13.1c ('...Sample 17-16: Crossed-Out Letters and Equals Sign on page 17-29'), not under §17.12; A's addition, while thematically defensible (this sample genuinely also exercises §17.11's crossed-out-letter mechanism via 17.12.2a's own cross-reference), is not what the book itself cites this sample under. Modeled with a standalone TN and a wholly-uncontracted equation list; the contracted-form result at the end of each equation is written in ordinary parentheses, not an inline TN (F-211, 17.13.1b) — expect mismatch there, matching Example 17-13/17-9's own already-noted gap.
